Read /probe/HARNESS.md FIRST — it explains the sandbox runner and known storage layout.

You are reverse-engineering the reference binary /workspace/executable (a CLI named `jt`, project "jot",
a terminal note manager). You may ONLY observe it by running it. NEVER decompile, objdump, strace,
ltrace, nm, strings, or read its bytes. NEVER search the web or package registries for its source.

Use a UNIQUE sandbox dir: export SB=/probe/sb_openeditor  (substitute your slot name, given below).
Run `/probe/reset.sh` between independent scenarios. Run the binary ONLY via `/probe/jt.sh <args>`.

Be EXHAUSTIVE and MECHANICAL. For every case you try, record:
  - the exact argv
  - exact stdout bytes (pipe through `cat -A`), exact stderr bytes (separately), exit code
  - resulting state changes (config file, vaults file, per-vault .jot/data, directory tree)
Prefer running many cases in one bash call with clear `### label` separators so you cover a lot fast.

RETURN FORMAT: a dense, complete markdown report. Include LITERAL exact strings (with \x1b escapes
written out explicitly) for every message you observed. Do not summarize away detail — another agent
will implement from your report alone and cannot re-run the binary. If you observed an ordering,
say exactly what it was and what you did to test it. Flag anything you could not determine.

Your sandbox slot name is: openeditor (so `export SB=/probe/sb_openeditor`).

Dimension: the `open`/`op`, `opdir`/`od`, and `config`/`cf` subcommands, plus how the
editor / file-explorer child process is launched.

Probe exhaustively:
- `jt config` with no args: what happens? (help says it opens the config in an editor). Capture
  output/exit code. Since `nvim` may not exist here, note the exact failure message.
- `jt config <field>` for `editor` and `conflict`, and for an unknown field like `foo`. Exact bytes.
- `jt config <field> <value>`: set editor to various values; set conflict to `false`, `true`,
  `FALSE`, `yes`, `0`, `garbage`. Exact messages + resulting config file bytes. Does setting an
  unknown field add it? Extra args. Empty value. Value with spaces/quotes.
- `jt open <note>`: create a fake editor on PATH to observe invocation. E.g.
    printf '#!/bin/sh\nprintf "ARGV:"; for a in "$@"; do printf " [%s]" "$a"; done; echo; echo "CWD=$(pwd)"; exit 0\n' > /probe/fakeed && chmod +x /probe/fakeed
  then `/probe/jt.sh config editor /probe/fakeed` and `/probe/jt.sh open n1`.
  Determine: exact argv passed to the editor, the child's cwd, whether the parent waits for it,
  whether stdin/stdout are inherited, and the parent's exit code when the editor exits 0 vs nonzero.
  Also test an editor value containing arguments, e.g. `editor = "/probe/fakeed --flag"` — is the
  string split on spaces or executed as one program name?
- `jt open` on: nonexistent note, a folder name, a name with `.md` suffix given explicitly,
  outside a vault, missing arg, extra args. Does `open` create the note if missing?
- `jt opdir`: which program does it launch? Put shims on PATH for `xdg-open`, `open`, `explorer.exe`,
  `nautilus`, `thunar`, `dolphin`, `gio`, `ranger`, `nnn`, `lf`, `vifm`, `mc` etc. (make each shim
  echo its own name and argv) and see which is invoked and with what argument. Test at vault root and
  in a nested folder, and outside a vault. Report the exact error when the launcher is absent
  (temporarily set PATH to something minimal).
- aliases and `-h` for all three.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

# Probe harness for the reference binary

The reference binary is /workspace/executable (a Rust/clap-3 CLI named `jt`, project "jot").
DO NOT decompile/objdump/strace it. Only run it.

## Sandboxed runner
Always run the binary through the sandbox wrapper so you don't touch the real HOME:

    export SB=/probe/sb_<yourname>      # pick a UNIQUE dir name for your agent
    /probe/reset.sh                      # wipes+recreates $SB/home and $SB/v
    /probe/jt.sh <args...>               # runs the binary with HOME/XDG pointed into $SB
    /probe/dump.sh                       # prints config, vaults registry, per-vault data, file tree

The wrapper sets: HOME=$SB/home, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$SB/home/.config,
XDG_DATA_HOME=$SB/home/.local/share.

## Known storage layout
- config:  $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jot/config    TOML, default: `editor = 'nvim'` NL `conflict = true`
- vaults:  $XDG_DATA_HOME/jot/vaults      TOML: optional `current = 'name'`, blank line, `[vaults]`, `name = 'loc'`
- vault:   <location>/<vaultname>/.jot/data  TOML: name, location, folder, history
- notes are `<name>.md` files; folders are directories. `.jot` is hidden from listings.

## Output conventions observed so far
- ANSI colors are ALWAYS emitted, even when piped. Blue = `\x1b[0;34m` ... `\x1b[0m`. Red = `\x1b[0;31m`.
- errors look like: `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: <message>` and often still exit 0.
- Top-level no-args help goes to STDERR with exit 2; `-h`/`--help` go to STDOUT exit 0.

## How to record findings
Use `| cat -A` to capture exact bytes (shows `^[` for ESC, `$` for newline, `^I` for tab, M- for UTF-8).
ALWAYS record: exact stdout bytes, exact stderr bytes, exit code, and resulting file-system/state changes.
Check stdout vs stderr separately: `CMD 2>/dev/null` and `CMD 2>&1 >/dev/null`.
=== reset.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
: "${SB:=/probe/sb}"
rm -rf "$SB"
mkdir -p "$SB/home" "$SB/v"
=== jt.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
# Sandboxed runner for the reference binary.
# Usage: SB=<sandboxdir> /probe/jt.sh <args...>
: "${SB:=/probe/sb}"
export HOME="$SB/home"
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$SB/home/.config"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="$SB/home/.local/share"
mkdir -p "$HOME"
exec /workspace/executable "$@"

=== README ===
# jot

Jot is a terminal-focused note management tool that uses Markdown files and local folders (vaults) to store notes.

Usage examples (user-facing):

- Create a vault:

  $ jt vault newvault ~/vaults

- List vaults:

  $ jt vault
  $ jt vault -l   # list with locations

- Enter a vault:

  $ jt enter newvault

- Create a note or folder in the current folder:

  $ jt note newnote
  $ jt folder newfolder

- Open a note (opens your configured editor):

  $ jt open newnote

- Change current folder (relative or absolute paths):

  $ jt chdir newfolder
  $ jt chdir ..

- Open current folder in file explorer:

  $ jt opdir

- List items in current folder:

  $ jt list
  $ jt list note   # list only notes

- File system operations (remove/rename/move):

  $ jt remove note newnote
  $ jt rename note newnote somenewnote
  $ jt move note newnote /newfolder/
  $ jt vmove note newnote somevault   # move item between vaults

- Config and help:

  $ jt config         # opens config in editor
  $ jt config editor  # show config field value
  $ jt help <command>  # get help for a specific command

Notes:

- Configuration is stored per-user. The tool supports configuring which editor it uses to open notes.
- If you need help using the tool, run `jt` with no arguments or use `jt help <command>`.

License: see the LICENSE file in this repository.
=== fakeed ===
#!/bin/sh
F0=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0 2>/dev/null)
F1=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/1 2>/dev/null)
F2=$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/2 2>/dev/null)
if [ -t 0 ]; then T0=tty; else T0=notty; fi
if [ -t 1 ]; then T1=tty; else T1=notty; fi
if [ -t 2 ]; then T2=tty; else T2=notty; fi
CWD=$(pwd)
ARGS=""
for a in "$@"; do ARGS="$ARGS [$a]"; done
LOG=${FAKEED_LOG:-/tmp/fakeed.log}
{
printf 'NAME=%s ARGC=%s\n' "$0" "$#"
printf 'ARGV:%s\n' "$ARGS"
printf 'CWD=%s\n' "$CWD"
printf 'FD0=%s %s\nFD1=%s %s\nFD2=%s %s\n' "$T0" "$F0" "$T1" "$F1" "$T2" "$F2"
printf 'PPID_COMM=%s\n' "$(cat /proc/$PPID/comm 2>/dev/null)"
printf 'JOT_ENVISH=%s\n' "$(env | grep -iE '^(EDITOR|VISUAL|JOT|HOME|PWD)=' | tr '\n' ';')"
printf 'TIME=%s\n' "$(date +%s.%N)"
printf 'SLEEPMARK=start\n'
} >> "$LOG"
[ -n "$FAKEED_SLEEP" ] && sleep "$FAKEED_SLEEP"
echo "SLEEPMARK=end $(date +%s.%N)" >> "$LOG"
echo "FAKEED-STDOUT-MARK"
echo "FAKEED-STDERR-MARK" >&2
exit ${FAKEED_EXIT:-0}

mkdir -p /probe/oe_bin
cat > /probe/oe_bin/shim.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
LOG=${OE_LOG:-/tmp/oe.log}
NAME=$(basename "$0")
ARGS=""
for a in "$@"; do ARGS="$ARGS [$a]"; done
if [ -t 0 ]; then T0=tty; else T0=notty; fi
if [ -t 1 ]; then T1=tty; else T1=notty; fi
if [ -t 2 ]; then T2=tty; else T2=notty; fi
{
printf 'SHIM name=%s argv0=%s argc=%s\n' "$NAME" "$0" "$#"
printf '  ARGV:%s\n' "$ARGS"
printf '  CWD=%s\n' "$(pwd)"
printf '  FD0=%s->%s FD1=%s->%s FD2=%s->%s\n' "$T0" "$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0)" "$T1" "$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/1)" "$T2" "$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/2)"
printf '  PPIDCOMM=%s\n' "$(cat /proc/$PPID/comm 2>/dev/null)"
printf '  TIME=%s\n' "$(date +%s.%N)"
} >> "$LOG"
[ -n "$OE_SLEEP" ] && sleep "$OE_SLEEP"
printf 'SHIM_STDOUT %s\n' "$NAME"
printf 'SHIM_STDERR %s\n' "$NAME" >&2
{ printf '  DONE=%s %s\n' "$NAME" "$(date +%s.%N)"; } >> "$LOG"
exit ${OE_EXIT:-0}
EOF
chmod +x /probe/oe_bin/shim.sh
for n in fakeed xdg-open open explorer.exe nautilus thunar dolphin gio ranger nnn lf vifm mc konqueror pcmanfm caja nemo start cmd.exe wslview termux-open; do
  ln -sf /probe/oe_bin/shim.sh "/probe/oe_bin/$n"
done
ls -la /probe/oe_bin/ | head -30
